newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian Dubrovacka plans new share issue, listing.
newsitem.headline: Croatian Dubrovacka plans new share issue, listing.

text.p: Croatia's Dubrovacka Banka said on Wednesday its shareholders approved a new share issue, designed to raise its capital by 140 million kuna to just under 320 million.
This may improve the bank's position among Croatia's commercial banks where it ranked 12th according to capital in 1995, and boost its competitiveness.
Dubrovacka is mulling plans to sell up to 50 percent of the new stock abroad, most likely on the London Stock Exchange, board member Petar Skurla said.
It would make it the second banking institution from Croatia, after Zagrebacka Banka to do so.
"We are about to close a deal with the London bank Lazard Capital Markets," Skurla told Reuters by telephone from the southern coastal town of Dubrovnik, where the bank is based.
The offering could take place within the next 2-3 months, he said.
The new issue will be split into 20,000 ordinary C-series shares with a face value of 7,000 kuna each -- the same as Dubrovacka's outstanding ordinary stock.
The bank is planning to list its shares on the Zagreb Stock Exchange before the end of 1997, Skurla said and added:
"After this we would begin preparations for a listing in London, probably for next year."
Dubrovacka last week reported a pre-tax profit slump to 18.6 million kuna in 1996 from over 57 million a year earlier, after allotting more for risk provisions in a bid to consolidate further.
Holders of its bearer stock will receive a dividend of 23 percent on face value -- some 115 kuna -- on 1996 results. This is unchanged from 1995, Skurla said.
But the bank will again skip dividend on the ordinary shares, he added.
Dubrovacka has outstanding 25,036 ordinary shares with a nominal price of 7,000 kuna and 9,054 preferred bearer shares, issued at 500 kuna each. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
